'''Slavko Vraneš''' ({{lang-sr-cyrl|Славко Вранеш}}, {{IPA|sh|slǎːvkɔ̝ vrâne̞ːʃ|pron}}; born 30 January 1983) is a Montenegrin former professional [[basketball]] player. Standing at {{height|m=2.29}},<ref name="RealGMSV">[http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Slavko-Vranes/Summary/472 Realgm.com profile]</ref><ref name="ABASV">[https://www.aba-liga.com/player.php?id=184 ABA League profile]</ref><ref name="ELSV">[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=BGJ Euroleague.net profile]</ref> he was one of the tallest players in the world. While he only played one game in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) in his career, a 2004 regular season game for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], he went on to have a successful career in [[Europe]], winning the [[2011 Eurocup Basketball Final Four|2011 EuroCup]] with [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]]. Internationally, Vraneš represented the [[Montenegro national basketball team|Montenegrin national team]].

==Professional career==
Vraneš started playing basketball in the Serbian club [[KK FMP (1991–2011)|FMP Železnik]]. Still a junior, he was snapped up by the Turkish club [[Efes Pilsen S.K.|Efes Pilsen]] for the 2000–01 season. Then he returned to his native country in January 2001,<ref>[http://arhiva.glas-javnosti.rs/arhiva/2001/01/25/srpski/S01012403.shtml Vraneš naš do 24. godine]</ref> where he played for [[KK Budućnost Podgorica|Budućnost Podgorica]] until the summer of 2003.

Vraneš was selected by the [[National Basketball Association]]'s [[New York Knicks]] in the second round of the [[2003 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=Greg Logan |title=Knicks' Big Catch |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98157345/knicks-big-catch/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Newsday]] |date=28 June 2003 |page=30|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Marc Berman |title=Don sees promise in Vranes |url=https://nypost.com/2003/07/20/don-sees-promise-in-vranes/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=20 July 2003}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Steve Popper |title=Knicks Being Patient With Vranes |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/07/20/sports/basketball/knicks-being-patient-with-vranes.html |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[New York Times]] |date=20 July 2003}}</ref> He was waived by the Knicks in December 2003 before ever playing a game for them.<ref>{{cite news |title=Thomas, Knicks waive center Slavko Vranes |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98157569/thomas-knicks-waive-center-slavko/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Ventura County Star]] |date=25 December 2003 |page=C2}}</ref> 

In early January 2004, he signed a ten-day contract with [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. Before his contract with Portland expired, he played one game on January 8, which became Vraneš's only career NBA game. The game was a 75–96 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], where Vraneš played for three minutes and recorded one foul and one missed field goal..<ref name=bbr>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/v/vranesl01.html|title=Slavko Vraneš NBA stats|website=[[Basketball Reference]]|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|accessdate=6 June 2024}}</ref>

After that, he played briefly for [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]]. From 2004 to 2007, he played with [[KK Budućnost Podgorica|Budućnost Podgorica]] for the second time in his career. In October 2007, he signed a three-year contract with [[KK Partizan|Partizan]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/15925/180/item Partizan inks giant Slavko Vranes]</ref>

In October 2011, he signed with [[Petrochimi Bandar Imam BC|Sanaye Petroshimi BC]] in the [[Iranian Basketball Super League|Iranian Super League]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/31468/slavko_vranes_moves_to_sanaye_petroshimi_bc_in_iran.html Slavko Vranes moves to Sanaye Petroshimi BC in Iran]</ref> During 2013, he played with [[KK Metalac Valjevo|Metalac Valjevo]]. In October 2013 he signed with [[Zob Ahan Isfahan BC|Zob Ahan Isfahan]].<ref>{{cite web|title=BC Zob Ahan signs giant Slavko Vranes|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/65836/bc-zob-ahan-signs-giant-slavko-vranes.html|publisher=Sportando.net|access-date=25 October 2013}}</ref>

On February 10, 2015, he re-signed with Metalac Valjevo.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/serbia/151852/slavko-vranes-moves-to-metalac.html Slavko Vranes moves to Metalac]</ref> On May 8, he left Metalac Valjevo.<ref>[http://www.eurobasket.com/Montenegro/news/403767/Slavko-Vranes-leaves-Metalac Slavko Vranes leaves Metalac]</ref> Later that month, he returned to his former team Petrochimi Bandar Imam of Iran.<ref>[http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2015&mm=05&dd=14&nav_id=991994 Metalac bez Vraneša, otišao u Iran] (Serbian)</ref>

In November 2017, he signed with Metalac Valjevo.<ref>[http://sport014.rs/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=1321:vranes-treci-put-u-metalcu&catid=22&Itemid=197 Vraneš treći put u Metalcu] {{in lang|sr}}</ref>
